title: Android Earthquake Alerts detects the Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake and alerts more than 16 million users on 23 April 2025
summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts detected the Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake of 23 April 2025 and alerted over 16 million users, but its stronger alert missed inland areas of moderate shaking.
account: On 23 April 2025 the Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake, of moment magnitude (Mw) 6.2, struck offshore in the Sea of Marmara, Türkiye. Initial reports cited by the evaluation put shaking in Istanbul at intensity V on the Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) scale. At least 359 people were injured, mostly from panic. Google's Android Earthquake Alerts (AEA) system uses the accelerometers of online Android phones, and Google launched it in Türkiye in June 2021. An on-phone detection algorithm flags sudden changes in acceleration. The system detected the event 5.31 seconds after its origin. It issued a first “Be Aware” alert 0.43 seconds later on an initial magnitude estimate of Mw 4.83. “Take Action” alerts followed as the estimate rose. Alerts reached more than 16 million Android users in Türkiye, Greece, Romania and Bulgaria. The modeled warning distribution for residents in correctly alerted geographic areas of weak shaking (MMI III) reached up to 150 seconds, with a median of 56 seconds. The figures of 90% true positives and 99% precision also count people by geographic area. Neither figure counts alerted devices. In a separate voluntary survey of 67,056 recipients, 50.5% reported receiving a warning before they felt shaking. The final magnitude estimate saturated at Mw 6.04, so the “Take Action” polygon was too small. Inland populations that felt MMI V shaking received only the “Be Aware” warning before stronger shaking arrived. Google reports that more than 116 million alerts had been issued in Türkiye for 203 detected events between June 2021 and 16 September 2025. Google employees wrote the system description (Science, 17 July 2025) and the evaluation (Nature Communications, 11 August 2026), and the user-feedback data also come from Google. The same system underestimated the Türkiye earthquakes of 6 February 2023. The BBC reported on 27 July 2025 that only 469 “Take Action” alerts were sent for the magnitude 7.8 event, when 10 million people could have received one. The AI Incident Database records that underestimation as incident 1546.
purpose: Crowd-sourced earthquake detection and early warning delivered to Android phones in countries without dense seismic networks. The alerts were the intended use.
deployer: Google (alerts delivered directly to Android users; launched in Türkiye in June 2021)
location: Sea of Marmara / Istanbul region, Türkiye (alerts also in Greece, Romania and Bulgaria)
taxonomy_note: An earthquake warning is read as a detection mechanism; no averted injury is documented.

ratings.reason: Google's feedback data say that recipients were likely to drop, cover and hold on or to warn others. No individual injury avoided is documented, and Google collected the data.
No organization's decision or operation is documented as changed by the alerts.

More than 16 million users were alerted, with a median warning of 56 seconds for weak shaking. The “Take Action” alerts did not reach inland areas of moderate shaking (MMI V) in time. No reduction in injuries is demonstrated, and Google employees wrote the evidence.

ai_role.statement: The system itself generated the detection and the alerts. A few hundred phones triggered on the P wave. The system detected the event 5.31 s after origin and issued alerts within 0.43 s. Magnitude estimates were updated over the next 12 s. All performance figures and user-response data come from Google-authored papers (Mousavi et al. 2026; Allen et al. 2025). That is said plainly here. The only independent cited source, the BBC, concerns the 2023 underestimation. The read papers describe the detection as an on-phone algorithm that analyzes acceleration time series for sudden changes. They do not use the terms machine learning or artificial intelligence. Whether the system uses AI is not established by the sources.

fields.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts detected the Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake of 23 April 2025 and alerted over 16 million users, but its stronger alert missed inland areas of moderate shaking.
fields.account: On 23 April 2025 the Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake, of moment magnitude (Mw) 6.2, struck offshore in the Sea of Marmara, Türkiye. Initial reports cited by the evaluation put shaking in Istanbul at intensity V on the Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) scale. At least 359 people were injured, mostly from panic. Google's Android Earthquake Alerts (AEA) system uses the accelerometers of online Android phones, and Google launched it in Türkiye in June 2021. An on-phone detection algorithm flags sudden changes in acceleration. The system detected the event 5.31 seconds after its origin. It issued a first “Be Aware” alert 0.43 seconds later on an initial magnitude estimate of Mw 4.83. “Take Action” alerts followed as the estimate rose. Alerts reached more than 16 million Android users in Türkiye, Greece, Romania and Bulgaria. The modeled warning distribution for residents in correctly alerted geographic areas of weak shaking (MMI III) reached up to 150 seconds, with a median of 56 seconds. The figures of 90% true positives and 99% precision also count people by geographic area. Neither figure counts alerted devices. In a separate voluntary survey of 67,056 recipients, 50.5% reported receiving a warning before they felt shaking. The final magnitude estimate saturated at Mw 6.04, so the “Take Action” polygon was too small. Inland populations that felt MMI V shaking received only the “Be Aware” warning before stronger shaking arrived. Google reports that more than 116 million alerts had been issued in Türkiye for 203 detected events between June 2021 and 16 September 2025. Google employees wrote the system description (Science, 17 July 2025) and the evaluation (Nature Communications, 11 August 2026), and the user-feedback data also come from Google. The same system underestimated the Türkiye earthquakes of 6 February 2023. The BBC reported on 27 July 2025 that only 469 “Take Action” alerts were sent for the magnitude 7.8 event, when 10 million people could have received one. The AI Incident Database records that underestimation as incident 1546.
